question: In which state is the Jhumming cultivation known as Dahiya?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jhumming cultivation is a traditional form of shifting agriculture practiced in various states of India.
 
• In Madhya Pradesh, this form of agriculture is specifically known as Dahiya.
 
• It involves clearing a piece of land by cutting down and burning vegetation, then cultivating crops on it for a few years before moving to a new area.
 
• Dahiya is practiced mainly by the tribal communities in the hilly regions of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• This method is part of the cultural heritage and agricultural practices of these tribal communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting Cultivation**

 
 
• It is an agricultural system in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned and allowed to revert to their natural vegetation.
 
• This cycle is repeated as the farmer moves to a new area.
 
• Shifting cultivation is also known as slash-and-burn agriculture.
 
• It is commonly practiced in tropical rainforests and hilly terrains.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Shifting cultivation can lead to deforestation and loss of biodiversity if not managed sustainably.
 
• It can also cause soil erosion and degradation over time.
 
• Sustainable practices are necessary to mitigate these environmental impacts.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Communities**
 
 
• Tribal communities in India often rely on traditional agricultural practices like shifting cultivation.
 
• These practices are deeply rooted in their cultural and social systems.
 
• Government policies and programs aim to support sustainable agricultural practices among tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Policies**
 
 
• The Indian government has various schemes to promote sustainable agriculture and support farmers.
 
• Programs focus on improving agricultural productivity, sustainability, and farmers' livelihoods.
 
• Efforts include providing training, financial assistance, and access to modern agricultural technologies.
